domain: recall — the diachronic gate (retrieval, admission, PER)
summary:
Recall precision is an EMPIRICAL BET, so the harness is built first and must be RED before any retrieval exists (PL-2). Order: harness → gold sets → model providers → cue synthesis → taxonomy/LMB → DDL+projection triggers → ANN arms → BM25 → fusion/admission → orchestrator+PER.

Headline decision (my domain's TRAPPOINT contribution): the C-SPANN prefix columns on event_cue_embedding/event_cue_coarse are PROJECTIONS written by a BEFORE INSERT trigger from the parent event_cue and event.severity_gate, never inputs. If an inserter picks the prefix it picks the K-means tree, and a fatality filed into the wrong tree is unreachable forever with no refusal anywhere — S1 one hop upstream, applied to the index partition.

Second: the ≤3 cap applies ONLY to origin='recall_probabilistic'; channels A and B are uncapped, else the cap contradicts bonded_fatalities_all_blocking (MI16).

Offline-first: bge-large-en-v1.5 (MIT, native 1024-d) + committed PCA for the 256-d coarse vector, so the harness and demo run with no AWS account; Titan v2 + Matryoshka is the live path. Reranker/cue synthesis = Claude on the au.* Bedrock profile, model id resolved at runtime, never hard-coded (PL-3).

τ = max(LTT bound, precision-floor) so a recall-driven threshold can never breach the nuisance ceiling. PER leaves use fixed-point integer scores with RFC-6962 domain separation. PER proves exhaustion of the retrieval that ran, not of the corpus — CI-grepped into every artefact.</summary>

workers.title: Evaluation harness — the RED gate for the whole domain
workers.brief:
You build the suite that every other recall worker is judged by, and it MUST be red when you finish. Read ARCHITECTURE.md §6.7 and §6.2-6.4, BUILD_PLAN.md K4 exit criteria G4α, research/05-architecture/diachronic-recall.md §7-8, and docs/leads/recall.md.

Create the uv workspace package packages/trappoint-recall (pyproject.toml with name trappoint-recall, Apache-2.0, python>=3.13, deps: pydantic>=2, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn; NO psycopg, NO boto3, NO mainline_* imports — import-linter enforces this), plus src/trappoint_recall/__init__.py, py.typed and README.md. Everything else you write lives under src/trappoint_recall/eval/.

Implement: metrics.py — Recall@1/@3/@10, nDCG@10, P@block (precision of blocking probabilistic checks on a blinded adjudicated subset), nuisance rate (share of routine permits producing >=1 probabilistic blocking check), mean blocking checks/permit, MRR and full rank distribution. Every metric returns a Measurement dataclass carrying point estimate, Wilson score interval lower and upper bound at 95%, n, and the split policy id — never a bare float. splits.py — temporally-blocked split construction with an explicit time wall t: candidates must satisfy occurred_at < t AND ingested_at < t AND corpus_commit <= t; a helper that REFUSES and raises if asked to use AS OF SYSTEM TIME (gc.ttlseconds is 4h). qrels.py — load/validate graded relevance judgements (0-3 UMBRELA scale) from JSONL, with a pydantic model and a JSON Schema emitted to the package. ablation.py — run a named configuration matrix (A, A+B, A+B+C, A+B+C+D, +rerank, +SGA; cue-vs-narrative; prefix on/off; 1024 vs 256; beam sweep) against a RetrievalBackend Protocol you define here (async def retrieve(query, k) -> list[ScoredCandidate]) and emit a markdown + JSON ablation table. report.py + cli.py — a `trappoint-recall-eval` console script.

Then write tests/eval/recall/: test_g4alpha_gates.py asserting Retro-Recall@3 on severity-5 >= 0.90 (Wilson LB >= 0.80), P@block >= 0.75, nuisance rate < 0.03, mean blocking checks/permit <= 1.0, and the L3 silence conservation law candidates == blocking + advisory + silenced + deduped exactly. These use a NullBackend that returns nothing, so they FAIL. Mark them with a `pytest.mark.g4alpha` marker and wire a CI lane that runs them and records red/green, never skipping. Also test_metrics_properties.py — Hypothesis property tests: Wilson LB <= point estimate <= UB; Recall@k monotone non-decreasing in k; nDCG in [0,1]; conservation law is exact integer arithmetic.

Finally scripts/recall/no_bare_point_estimates.py — a CI grep that fails if a recall metric appears in docs/, README.md or the deck without an interval alongside it.

Do NOT implement any retrieval, embedding, SQL or model call. Do not soften the gates to make them pass. A suite that has never been red asserts nothing about a product whose deliverable is a refusal.

workers.title: Corpora and the four gold sets, plus the THYMOGATE panel
workers.brief:

Write src/trappoint_recall/corpora/. msha.py — parse MSHA Part 50 bar-delimited accident/injury extracts (note: the NARRATIVE column is VARCHAR2(384), so Part 50 alone gives terse records; the rich text is in the fatality investigation reports) and the fatality-report PDF corpus into a normalised EventRecord model (external_ref, occurred_at, narrative, coded accident classification, injury source, mining method, equipment, severity_actual). csb.py — the same shape for CSB investigation reports and AU state regulator safety alerts. Severity is taken from coded fields or regulator classification ONLY — never model-rated; the loader raises if asked to infer it.

Gold sets: g1_citations.py — distant supervision from investigation reports that cite prior similar incidents; each citation is a human-authored (query event, relevant precursor) pair. Resolve citations by exact identifier match plus a verified anchor check; unresolvable citations are dropped with a logged count, never guessed. g2_codes.py — structured-code co-membership (same accident classification + injury source + equipment) as weak positives, labelled grade 1, explicitly marked calibrator-only and forbidden from headline metrics by a flag on the qrels file. g3_adjudicated.py — ~200 pairs, UMBRELA-style 0-3 pre-labelling with a human-confirmation workflow: emit an adjudication worksheet, ingest confirmations, and record inter-rater disagreement. LLM-only labels must be tagged and are refused by the P@block metric. g4_retro.py — THE money metric: for each severity-5 event at time t, synthesise the permit that would have preceded it from the investigation's own description of the work, and build a qrels file with the time wall t attached, using the splits helper (predicates, never AOST). negative_control.py — synthesise a 24-month replay of routine, uneventful permits for the nuisance-rate denominator. panel.py + thymogate.py — the M5 AIRE-promiscuous panel: a curated set of the fleet's known killers (one per hazard_energy class, mixed levels), plus a certificate emitter that runs a candidate retrieval configuration against the panel and produces a ThymogateCertificate (config digest, panel digest, per-item recalled/missed, verdict) — a configuration that misses any panel item cannot be certified.

CI must be fully hermetic — no network.

Write tests/eval/recall_corpora/test_goldset_invariants.py: no gold pair leaks across the time wall; G2 is flagged calibrator-only; severity is never model-rated; every qrels file validates against the schema; the panel covers all eight hazard_energy classes. IMPORTANT: real corpora are for the harness only — the demo tenant is synthetic, and a real fatality must never be presented as a fictional site's record. Enforce it with a fixture-provenance field checked in the test.

workers.title: Model providers — embeddings and the Claude judge, offline-first
workers.brief:

Define two Protocols. EmbeddingProvider: `embed(texts: list[str], facet: str) -> list[Vector1024]` and `coarse(vecs) -> list[Vector256]`, plus a stable `model_id` string and `index_gen` label. Implementations: BedrockTitanV2 (amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0, 1024-d, cosine; coarse = Matryoshka truncation to 256 then L2-renormalise CLIENT-SIDE) and LocalBGE (BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 pinned by revision sha, MIT, native 1024-d; coarse = a committed PCA projection matrix loaded from the package, NOT truncation — bge is not MRL-trained and truncating it would be a false claim). Both emit distinct model_id strings; a helper `assert_homogeneous(rows)` raises if a corpus mixes them.

JudgeProvider: `judge(system_blocks, user_payload, schema) -> ValidatedModel`. Implementation BedrockClaudeJudge targeting the au.* cross-region inference profile. The model id / profile ARN must be RESOLVED AT RUNTIME via bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles and returned in a ResolvedModel record that callers pin into recall_policy — never hard-code it (AWS credentials are not yet valid on this machine; PL-3 forbids an unproven capability on a dated path). A blanket-retry helper is banned. Check stop_reason BEFORE touching content; a refusal raises ModelRefusal so the caller writes silence_ledger(reason='model_refusal') — a precursor the model declined to summarise must still block the merge.

Prompt caching: expose a `system_blocks` API that places cache_control {type:'ephemeral'} on the last stable system block, with volatile content forced into the user turn. Provide `last_usage` so callers can assert cache_read_input_tokens.

Cassettes: a record/replay layer keyed by sha256 of the canonical request (JCS, sorted keys) writing to tests/fixtures/cassettes/recall/. Replay is the CI and demo default (env MAINLINE_RECALL_PROVIDER=cassette). Record mode requires explicit opt-in. Commit cassettes for the fixture corpus.

workers.title: Recurrence-Condition Cues — the symmetric write-time genre bridge
workers.brief:
You implement the single idea that makes cosine similarity mean something here: both sides emit the same four facets so query and document share a genre. Read ARCHITECTURE.md §5.4 (event_cue DDL and the paragraph on why embedding the narrative is wrong), §6.2, §8.4 prompt-injection posture, research/05-architecture/diachronic-recall.md §4, and docs/leads/recall.md D3/D6.

Write verticals/mainline/packages/mainline-recall-agent/src/mainline_recall_agent/cue/ only. Use the JudgeProvider from ../providers/ — do not call Bedrock or anthropic directly.

Schema: a strict Pydantic model with exactly five fields — mechanism, precondition, control_failure, recurrence_test (each <=60 tokens) and narrative (raw text, unchanged, the safety net). Each of the four synthesised facets has its own explicit `insufficient_evidence` escape: the model may return {facet: null, insufficient: true} per facet and MUST NOT invent one. A facet marked insufficient produces no cue row and a logged reason — never a placeholder string.

Two entry points with ONE prompt family: synthesise_event_cue(event, activity_path, asset_class) and synthesise_exposure_cue(permit, isolation_plan, clause_diff). The permit side derives its facets from permit fields, the isolation plan, and the diff of clauses being waived or weakened. Both must produce structurally identical output; a test asserts the two prompts share the same facet definitions block byte-for-byte (that block is also the cached system prefix).

Embedding text template (D3), implemented once and used by both sides: `f"{activity_path} | {asset_class} | {facet}: {cue_text}"`. Export `EMBED_TEMPLATE_SHA256` computed over the template plus the facet-definition block; callers pin it into recall_policy. A test asserts the constant matches a committed golden value so drift is a CI failure.

Anchor verification (injection-posture layer 4, the cheapest high-value control we have): a pure regex + gazetteer extractor for equipment tags, SI-normalised setpoints, regulatory citations and CAS numbers. Any cue whose hard anchors are ABSENT from the source document's extracted anchor set is REJECTED before insert and routed to human review with the offending span hash. Deterministic, no model involvement.

Provenance on every cue: is_derived=true, gen_model, prompt_version, source_span computed by an exact unique find() into the canonical text — we compute offsets, we never trust a model-reported offset. Overlapping or unresolvable spans fail the step rather than silently dropping text.

Refusal and dead-letter handling: catch ModelRefusal and DeadLetter from the provider and return a CueOutcome carrying the silence-ledger reason ('model_refusal' / 'abstained') for the orchestrator to write. Never swallow.

Tests: tests/unit/recall_cue/ — per-facet insufficient_evidence round-trips; anchor rejection fires on a cue citing a tag absent from the source; span offsets are exact and unique; template digest matches golden; the two prompts share the facet block. tests/eval/recall_cue/ — a cue-vs-narrative comparison harness stub that the ablation runner can call (report only, no threshold).
workers.done_when: Against the committed cassettes, both synthesise_event_cue and synthesise_exposure_cue emit schema-valid five-facet output with per-facet insufficient_evidence honoured, EMBED_TEMPLATE_SHA256 matches the committed golden value, and a cue citing an equipment tag absent from its source is rejected before insert.

workers.title: Functional taxonomy induction and Level-Materialised Bonds
workers.brief:
You build the archival spine that IS the vector-index prefix. Read ARCHITECTURE.md §5.4 (activity_node DDL, the Level-Materialised Bonds paragraph — this is the correction that makes the ancestor walk non-vacuous — and event_bond), research/05-architecture/diachronic-recall.md §3, and docs/leads/recall.md.

Write verticals/mainline/packages/mainline-recall-agent/src/mainline_recall_agent/taxonomy/ only. You consume mainline.activity_node and mainline.event (owned by the ancestry/ingest lead). If those migrations are not present, run against the fixture DDL you commit under tests/fixtures/recall_taxonomy/ and mark the integration lane skipped — never fake the table.

Level 1 is FROZEN and anchored to the buyer's ICMM Material Unwanted Event register: commit tests/fixtures/recall_taxonomy/icmm_mue_l1.json (12-25 codes) and a loader that refuses to write a level-1 node not present in it, and refuses any level-1 row with frozen=false. Prefix values are baked into the physical index, so re-inducting level 1 is a re-partition, not an update — the loader raises with that message.

Induction for levels 2-3 follows TnT-LLM's two phases via the JudgeProvider: sample ~2k narratives, propose per-document activity labels under a prompt constraint that a label must name a FUNCTION PERFORMED, never a thing or a place (a validator rejects labels matching a noun-phrase gazetteer of equipment/place terms); iterative merge/refine; freeze and version; then bulk-assign with a cheap deterministic classifier (TF-IDF + linear model, fitted on the model labels, committed as coefficients not a pickle); hold out 300 documents for human confirmation with acceptance thresholds >=0.85 top-1 at file level and >=0.95 at fonds level, reported with Wilson bounds via the eval package.

The taxonomy version is a commit: every induction run emits a TaxonomyVersion record (taxonomy_ver, parent version, label diff, model, prompt_version, holdout scores) and every bond written records taxonomy_ver. A re-induction silently changes what the gate would have recalled and that must be attributable — make the diff a first-class artefact.

LMB writer — the load-bearing part. For each event, resolve its archival path fonds/series/file and emit ONE event_cue row per level (scope_id set to each, scope_level 1/2/3) for every populated facet. This grades tree sizes (fonds large, file small) and makes the matching level a retrieval feature. A test asserts that an event at depth 3 with 4 populated facets produces exactly 12 cue rows with distinct (scope_id, facet) pairs, and that a level-1-only event produces exactly 4.

Bond writer for Channel B: populate mainline.event_bond (event_id, scope_id, taxonomy_ver, bond_basis in coded/llm_induced/human) for the event's node AND every ancestor, so 'a fatality never decays' is a set membership question and not a score. A test asserts ancestor closure: bonding to a file implies bonds to its series and fonds.

Tests in tests/unit/recall_taxonomy/: label validator rejects thing/place labels; level-1 loader refuses off-register and unfrozen rows; LMB row counts; bond ancestor closure; taxonomy diff is emitted and non-empty across two induction runs.

(1) fn_cue_prefix_project — BEFORE INSERT on event_cue_embedding AND on event_cue_coarse. It SELECTs site_id, scope_id, facet from mainline.event_cue (and severity_gate from mainline.event via event_cue.event_id) and OVERWRITES NEW.site_id/NEW.scope_id/NEW.facet/NEW.severity_gate regardless of what the inserter supplied, RAISING P0001 'MAINLINE: no parent cue — cannot place a vector in a prefix tree' when absent. workers.brief:

Part 1 — packages/trappoint-recall/src/trappoint_recall/fusion/ (Apache-2.0, pure functions, no DB, no model client):

mmr.py — Maximal Marginal Relevance dedup at lambda 0.7 over cue embeddings, returning the representative AND the suppressed siblings as an also_matched list. Siblings are visible, not hidden; the caller writes silence_ledger(reason='dedup_sibling') for each.
featurespec.py — a FROZEN, ordered feature vector: [rrf_score, best_arm_rank, scope_level, facet_onehot(5), rerank_verdict, rerank_confidence, control_class_overlap, asset_class_match, channel_mask, coarse_only]. domain: kernel — TRAPPOINT: the refusal engine (K1 THE REFUSAL + the K1-resident slices of K2)
summary:
The kernel is a spec + deterministic SQL templates + a conformance suite; everything else exists to make those three provable. Six strategy calls:
1. Ship a REFERENCE VERTICAL (`trappoint_ref`) from day one so K1 never depends on K3's blame closure, and the two-binding substrate claim is exercised the day it is written rather than at K12.
2. P2 becomes a compile-time refusal: `vertical.toml` must declare an `authority_source` for every projected gate column, and `trappoint render` refuses to emit a gate without one. Adversarial finding S1 becomes a build error.
3. Red-before-green is mechanical: W2 lands `db.yml` + CF-01 against an empty database and the run is observed RED; each later worker turns only the cases its brief names.
4. Refusal is a product surface: `spec/errors.md` (SQLSTATE contract), `spec/wire/refusal.md` (payload schema), and QUICKREFUSE — MUS/NAA computed with the DATABASE as the oracle over savepoint probes, so the explanation cannot disagree with the refusal.
5. Unwelding is mutation testing applied to invariants; output is `REFUSAL_DEPTH.md`; depth 1 means cut the mechanism, not ship it.
6. Every unproven GT-* capability is a render-time switch with committed fallback SQL, never a runtime branch (PL-3 made mechanical).
Four corrections to residual drift shipped as rulings: merge_record's partial-FK pair is MATCH SIMPLE with nullable permit_id/cr_id; disposition and override_ledger become subject-polymorphic (S16 left them permit-only, which bricks MI30); a missing clearance_legal row must let the REAL fk_clearance fire rather than a synthetic 23503 with no constraint name; no CASE expression in any PL/pgSQL body.
key_decisions: REFERENCE VERTICAL (`trappoint_ref` schema, in `packages/trappoint-sql/refvertical/`) ships at K1 — the kernel's conformance gate runs against it, so K1 is independent of K3's `clause_blame_closure`, and the substrate claim is proved two milestones early instead of asserted.

AUTHORITY SOURCE CONTRACT: `vertical.toml` must declare relation+key+columns+`on_missing="raise"` for every projected gate column; `trappoint render` REFUSES to emit a gate template whose projection has no declared authority. P2 / adversarial finding S1 becomes a build error rather than a code-review discipline.

D1 — `merge_record` carries nullable `permit_id`/`cr_id` plus two composite FKs; the '§5.5 partial-FK pair' is MATCH SIMPLE semantics made explicit (a composite FK with any NULL column is not enforced). `subject_id` stays NOT NULL, bound by `CHECK (subject_id = COALESCE(permit_id, cr_id))`.

D2 — `disposition` and `override_ledger` become subject-polymorphic (`subject_kind` + nullable `permit_id`/`cr_id` + exactly-one CHECK), mirroring `blocking_check`. §5.5's `disposition.permit_id NOT NULL` predates S16 and as written makes a change_request that trips `weaken_over_blood` permanently un-mergeable.

D3 — a missing `clearance_legal` row must NOT raise a synthetic `23503`. `fn_disposition_project` projects the STRICTEST requirements (`req_*=true`, `min_signer_rank=9`) and returns NEW so the REAL composite FK `fk_clearance` fires with its constraint name. The constraint name is the exhibit; a synthetic SQLSTATE has none, and a NULL projection would emit `23502`, outside the taxonomy.

D4 — no `CASE` expression in any PL/pgSQL body; counter arithmetic uses boolean casts (`+ (NOT NEW.reading_floor_met)::INT8`). GT-13 has not answered CASE-expression legality inside PL/pgSQL and PL-3 forbids a dated path on an unproven capability.

D5 — every GT-gated capability is a RENDER-TIME switch with committed fallback SQL, never a runtime branch: `binding.capabilities.stored_digest` (GT-13) and `binding.capabilities.triggerdef` (GT-05). `trappoint render` refuses to run without a `g1-attestation.json` marking each capability PASS or FALLBACK-SELECTED.

D6 — `trappoint migrate bootstrap` owns a `trappoint` schema (`schema_migration`, `schema_lock`, `schema_attestation`) outside the numbered sequence; kernel procedures live there too (`trappoint.merge_permit()`). CockroachDB has no advisory locks, so a real lock table is required.

D7/D8 — §18 numbering preserved; a slot needing more than one statement takes a lowercase letter suffix (`0071a`, `0071b`), the runner ordering lexicographically. Function range extends to 0100–0119 and trigger range to 0120–0149 (§18 was sized before `merge_change_request`, `explain_refusal` and the CAS helper existed).

D9/D10 — the outbox insert in `fn_check_materialised` is conditional on `binding.emit_outbox` (the substrate must not hard-depend on a changefeed table another lead owns); and `CREATE SEQUENCE`/`nextval(`/`SERIAL`/`unique_rowid()` are banned by a `trappoint migrate lint` CI guard, because the gap-free-by-CAS claim is worthless if one future migration reintroduces a sequence.

QUICKREFUSE — the I14 minimal-unsatisfiable-subset emitter uses the DATABASE as the MUS oracle: declarative counter decomposition first (deterministic, no probe), QuickXplain over `SAVEPOINT`/`ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` probes for composite refusals. MUS extraction with a SAT solver is prior art; using the RDBMS constraint engine that produced the refusal as the oracle that explains it is not, and it guarantees explanation and refusal cannot disagree.

The conformance suite is profile-parameterised (`--profile mainline` | `--profile trappoint-ref`) and driven by a machine-readable `spec/conformance/manifest.toml`; `ANOMALY_COVERAGE.md` and `REFUSAL_DEPTH.md` are generated from it, and a totality test fails CI on any case present in the manifest but not the corpus, or vice versa.

workers.title: QUICKREFUSE: the minimal unsatisfiable subset and nearest admissible alternative, with the database as the oracle
workers.brief: You build invariant I14 — 'every refusal emits an irreducible reason set and, where computable, the nearest admissible alternative'. Two algorithms, in this order. (1) DECLARATIVE DECOMPOSITION — primary, deterministic, sub-millisecond, no probe. Given a `GateRefused` naming a constraint, map the constraint to its counter (`gate_closed_when_issued → open_blocking`, `identity_conserved_when_issued → open_residue`, `conflicts_resolved_when_issued → open_conflicts`, `no_open_warrant_when_issued → open_warrants`, `boundary_certified_when_issued → unmodelled_asset_count`, `reading_floor_when_issued → unmet_floor_count/countersigned_count`, `fk_clearance → (virulence, kind)`, `epoch_pin_* → gate_epoch`) and resolve the WITNESS ROWS behind it — the exact `check_id`s, `clause_uuid`s and `precursor_event_id`s that are non-zero. That set is the MUS for every single-counter refusal, and the NAA is the minimum-cardinality set of obligations whose disposition restores admissibility, plus (for `fk_clearance`) the set of `kind` values that DO exist at that `virulence` in `clearance_legal`. Implement the resolution as the `trappoint.explain_refusal(subject_kind, subject_id, constraint_name)` UDF returning JSONB so it is one round trip and EXPLAIN-assertable. (2) QUICKXPLAIN OVER SAVEPOINT PROBES — the general algorithm for composite refusals the decomposition does not cover. CockroachDB supports general-purpose nested savepoints and `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`, so run the classic divide-and-conquer QuickXplain with the DATABASE ITSELF as the oracle: `SAVEPOINT p; <apply candidate subset>; <attempt the transition>; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT p`. Because the oracle is the same constraint engine that produced the refusal, the explanation cannot disagree with it — that is the whole point, and it is the part with no prior art. Six hard constraints. (a) The probe transaction is SEPARATE from the gate transaction and is rolled back unconditionally in a `finally`; a refusal diagnosis must NEVER be able to mutate the gate. (b) Cap oracle calls (default 32) and degrade to the declarative MUS with `naa: null, reason: "probe_budget_exhausted"` rather than blocking. (c) Row locks are PRESERVED across `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` in CockroachDB (unlike PostgreSQL) — hold the probe transaction open for the minimum time and never probe on the merge path. (d) Emit only what the schema allows: NEVER a score, threshold or flag characterising a named human (I15 — the Allegation Firewall); `signer_sub` may appear as a fact, never as a metric. (e) `refusal_ledger` is append-only (`fn_refuse_mutation` applies) and stores the constraint name verbatim, because the constraint name is the exhibit. (f) 100% branch coverage on the MUS minimality property, asserted with a pure-Python oracle over synthetic constraint sets — no database needed for that test. Constraints: do NOT modify `trappoint-core`, do NOT write conformance cases, do not touch `spec/`.

key_decisions: A1 — No agent framework in Cognition. Single-shot zero-tool schema-constrained calls only. A2 — The only tool loops are the Steward (headless Claude Code + Managed MCP + Agent Skills) and the auditor's own agent; neither is Python on the merge path, and both sit in the plane that cannot write a gate-visible field.

A3 — Transport is boto3 `bedrock-runtime` InvokeModel with the Anthropic native body (anthropic_version bedrock-2023-05-31) and an `au.*` inference-profile ARN as modelId. NOT AnthropicBedrockMantle (different endpoint host, unverified policy surface) and NOT Converse (cannot express output_config.format). The residency control is a VPC-endpoint policy enumerating au.* ARNs on bedrock-runtime.

A4 — One model generation fleet-wide (claude-opus-5 via its au.* profile), differentiated by output_config.effort: low for triage/extraction, high for adjudication/NLI, xhigh for listwise rerank. Haiku triage rejected as default: Opus-5's minimum cacheable prefix is 512 tokens vs Haiku 4.5's 4096, and one model id means one profile ARN in the endpoint policy and one 403 path.

A5 — thinking is always explicit {"type":"adaptive"}, never omitted and never disabled. A6 — No sampling parameters anywhere; a repo-wide grep bans temperature/top_p/top_k. They 400 on this generation, and the honest claim was always replayability plus arithmetic reproducibility, never reproducibility.

A7 — bedrock_schema() derives the output_config JSON Schema from Pydantic, stripping the documented-unsupported keywords (maxLength/minLength, minimum/maximum/multipleOf, array-size constraints, recursion) and forcing additionalProperties:false; the stripped invariants become client-side validators. A8 — Refusal is silence and silence is a row: check stop_reason before content, branch on stop_reason only (stop_details may be null), write silence_ledger(outcome='silenced', reason='model_refusal'), fall back client-side. Server-side `fallbacks` is unavailable on Bedrock.

AWS creds are not yet valid, so E1/E2 run over a committed OpenTofu plan JSON and become live in cloud-verify.yml the day they are.

A16 — Upstream contribution targets an EMPTY domain: verifying-a-restore-by-merkle-root into cockroachdb-resilience-and-disaster-recovery (verified 2026-08-05: still .gitkeep-only). Define a `Renderer` protocol with `render(node, prompt_version) -> dict` and three implementations. `authored` reads the verbatim fixtures from fixtures/corpus/authored/ — this tier covers every camera-facing node and needs no model. `bedrock` calls boto3 `bedrock-runtime.converse` against `au.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` with strict tool use (a single tool whose input_schema has additionalProperties:false and every field required), temperature 0, top_p 1, fixed maxTokens, region ap-southeast-2. `template` is a deterministic offline renderer that composes prose from the skeleton plus the gazetteer plus the dated vocabulary-drift substitution schedule, so the corpus is complete with zero model calls.

The cache is the product here. Key = sha256(canonical_prompt ‖ model_id ‖ prompt_version). You add modules to packages/trappoint-verify. You own asn1.py and checks/{signature,tsa,beacon,witness,archive,attestation,webauthn}.py plus tests/crypto/ and tests/fixtures/. You do NOT edit pyproject.toml, cli.py, bundle.py, report.py, checks/__init__.py, checks/structural.py or vendor/ — worker 6 owns those. Register your checks through the registry hook checks/__init__.py exposes.

asn1.py: a minimal, strict, ~250-line DER reader (tag/length/value, definite lengths only, INTEGER, OCTET STRING, OID, UTCTime, GeneralizedTime, SEQUENCE, SET, explicit/implicit tagging). It must reject indefinite lengths, non-minimal lengths and trailing bytes. This exists because cryptography has NO CMS SignedData verification API — only PKCS#7 certificate extraction and decryption — and adding asn1crypto or rfc3161ng would break the one-dependency floor (CU-8).

checks/tsa.py: RFC 3161 TimeStampToken verification (check 5). Parse the CMS ContentInfo -> SignedData -> eContent (id-ct-TSTInfo) and extract messageImprint, genTime, serialNumber and policy; verify messageImprint equals SHA-256 of the checkpoint body; verify the SignerInfo signature over the DER re-encoding of signedAttrs (SET OF, not the implicit [0] form — this is the classic bug) using the embedded TSA certificate's public key via cryptography; check the certificate's validity window and its id-kp-timeStamping extended key usage; and pin the TSA certificate rather than attempting full chain validation, stating that limitation in the report. Provide scripts/custody/mint_local_tsa.py to generate an offline TSA CA + cert + genuine token as a test fixture, and scripts/custody/fetch_tsa_fixtures.py to pull real tokens from FreeTSA and the Sigstore TSA when network is available. Mark the real-token interop lane 'unverified' in the report until it runs green.

checks/signature.py (check 4): verify the C2SP note signature over the checkpoint body — ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 over DER per CU-3 — against a pinned SPKI, and optionally against a live kms:GetPublicKey response behind --kms-pubkey. checks/beacon.py (check 6): fully verify the NIST Beacon 2.0 pulse (RSA-PKCS#1v1.5 / SHA-512 over the canonical pulse field concatenation, certificate hash match) and verify drand quicknet's round->time arithmetic, reporting the BLS12-381 G1 signature as SKIP(optional-extra) unless an optional extra is installed — never claim to have verified it. checks/witness.py (check 7): >= q cosignatures over the SAME (tree_size, root), across distinct trust_domain values, at least one adverse=true; when q==1 over our own S3, the check reports PASS-but-not-adverse and the report says split-view resistance is NOT established. checks/archive.py (check 8): verify the recorded S3 object-version metadata in the bundle (bytes == body, ObjectLockMode == COMPLIANCE, LastModified inside the TSA/beacon bracket) offline, with live GetObjectVersion behind --s3. checks/attestation.py (check 11): the pg_get_triggerdef snapshot in schema_attestation matches the gate source shipped in the bundle — the self-attesting gate; if GT-05 forced the SHOW CREATE TABLE fallback, report PASS(coarse) and say why. checks/webauthn.py (check 12): re-verify the assertion against the enrolled COSE key (ES256 and RS256), reconstruct the challenge as SHA-256(receipt_digest || check_id || defeater_code || SHA-256(rationale) || disposition_kind || gate_epoch), verify clientDataJSON type/challenge/origin and the authenticatorData UV flag, and treat a sign_count regression as a WARNING, never a FAIL. Record CU-8 in docs/adr/0047-hand-rolled-rfc3161.md.
workers.done_when: A locally-minted RFC 3161 token verifies end to end (messageImprint, signedAttrs re-encoding, cert validity, id-kp-timeStamping) and a single-byte mutation anywhere fails it; the ASN.1 reader rejects indefinite lengths, non-minimal lengths and trailing bytes; a P-256 note signature verifies against a pinned SPKI; a NIST pulse verifies and drand reports SKIP(optional-extra); a q=1 witness set reports PASS-but-not-adverse; and a WebAuthn assertion re-verifies with a reconstructed challenge while a sign_count regression only WARNs. The dependency-floor test still passes.

workers.title: Anchor fanout behind protocols, and the indelible evidence stack with a policy merge gate
workers.brief:
Read ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 (the five anchoring steps), §10.1–10.3, §11.6 (crypto-shredding is document destruction; the KMS key policy denies ScheduleKeyDeletion and DisableKey except to a two-person break-glass role while any legal_hold is open), §19 GT-18; BUILD_PLAN.md K6 'fails how' (reuse the KMS key across rebuilds); docs/leads/custody.md CU-10 and CU-11. AWS credentials are NOT valid on this machine — design for AWS, do not block on it, and make every live path fail loudly rather than silently succeed wrong.

Build verticals/mainline/packages/mainline-anchor (FSL-1.1-ALv2): a fanout invoked per checkpoint. Every external system sits behind a typing.Protocol with an in-process fake used by tests — KmsSignPort, ObjectLockPort, TsaPort, BeaconPort, TilePublishPort, WitnessPushPort. The fakes ASSERT the exact call shape (PutObject with ObjectLockMode='COMPLIANCE' and a RetainUntilDate 7 years out plus ObjectLockLegalHoldStatus='ON'; kms:Sign with SigningAlgorithm='ECDSA_SHA_256'), so the first real invocation fails on a mismatch instead of writing an unlockable object. Order matters and must be tested: sign, then write to Object Lock, then acquire TSA tokens from >= 2 independent TSAs, then publish tiles, then push to witnesses over the changefeed webhook. Do NOT use moto for Object Lock — its enforcement is incomplete and a green test against a mock that does not enforce the control is worse than no test (CU-10).

Build infra/modules/evidence-store (OpenTofu/HCL): a versioned S3 bucket created WITH object_lock_enabled = true at creation (it cannot be retrofitted — GT-18 has no fallback), a default COMPLIANCE retention of 7 years, a bucket policy granting the write principal s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject ONLY, and a KMS ECC_NIST_P256 SIGN_VERIFY key whose policy allows kms:Sign to the sequencer role alone. Build infra/envs/evidence as a separate root module for the SECOND AWS account, with CloudTrail to a third account, and a justfile target that refuses `destroy` outright with an explanatory message (CU-11) — a rebuilt KMS key makes yesterday's ledger unverifiable, which is destruction committed by accident.

Build infra/policy/custody/*.rego and scripts/custody/check_evidence_plan.py as a MERGE GATE over `tofu show -json` plan output (accept a committed plan fixture when no credentials exist, so the gate runs today). It must FAIL on: a checkpoint bucket without object_lock_enabled at creation or without versioning; any write-account principal holding s3:DeleteObject, s3:DeleteObjectVersion, s3:PutObjectRetention, s3:PutObjectLegalHold or s3:BypassGovernanceRetention; kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion or kms:DisableKey grantable outside the break-glass role; a KMS key with a rotation or deletion schedule; and — enforcing GT-18's ordering — any OTHER root module in the repository declaring an S3 bucket that receives checkpoint objects. Commit at least one deliberately-failing plan fixture per rule so the gate is proven to bite. Record CU-11 in docs/adr/0048-indelible-evidence-stack.md.
workers.done_when: `python scripts/custody/check_evidence_plan.py` passes the compliant plan fixture and fails each deliberately-broken fixture with a distinct named rule; the anchor fanout test asserts sign-then-lock-then-timestamp-then-publish-then-push ordering and the exact ObjectLockMode='COMPLIANCE' and SigningAlgorithm='ECDSA_SHA_256' call shapes; `tofu validate` passes on both the module and the evidence root; and the destroy target refuses with a message.

workers.title: The C2SP tlog-witness cosigner, quorum admissibility, and custody of the custodian
workers.brief:
Read ARCHITECTURE.md §5.6 (cosignature, unwitnessed_debt, custodian_attestation), §7.3 items 4 and 5, §9.3 (ccloud), §5.10 (schema_attestation), §20 item 12; the C2SP tlog-witness and tlog-cosignature specifications; docs/leads/custody.md risk 1 and CU-9.

Build packages/trappoint-witness (Apache-2.0): the ~200-line C2SP tlog-witness service, Dockerised so the ask to an insurer, union HSR, external auditor or regulator is 'run this container', not 'build this'. It stores ONLY (origin, size, root) — roughly 100 bytes of state per log — accepts an add-checkpoint request, verifies the log's signature, verifies a consistency proof from its own last known state to the offered one, refuses on any inconsistency with a loud, specific error, and returns a cosignature line in signed-note form. It must refuse to sign a checkpoint smaller than its stored size and must be idempotent for a repeated identical checkpoint. Zero MAINLINE dependencies; state file is a single JSON document with an atomic replace. Include a README a non-engineer at a regulator can follow and a test that a split view — two different roots at the same tree size — is refused and recorded.

Implement the admissibility evaluator: a checkpoint is admissible only with >= k cosignatures across >= k distinct trust_domain values with at least one adverse = true, AND no open unwitnessed_debt row. Implement the debt reconciler: permits still merge when witnesses are unreachable (MAINLINE never blocks work on paperwork), each such merge inserts an unwitnessed_debt row, and no later checkpoint is admissible while debt is open; a retro-cosigned checkpoint discharges it. Test all four combinations, and test that the evaluator reports PASS-but-not-adverse when q == 1 over our own S3 — because that is today's honest state and split-view resistance must NOT be claimed.

Build verticals/mainline/packages/mainline-custody-patrol (FSL-1.1-ALv2) — custody of the custodian. It collects, on a schedule, the eight custodian_attestation kinds: ccloud_audit and ccloud_backup (consume the cloud lead's cc() wrapper through a Protocol with a fixture-backed fake; every call uses -o json and a missing field is a hard failure, never a default), inspect_database, schema_fingerprint, trigger_definitions, kms_key_policy, s3_object_lock and iam_snapshot. Each collection writes the full JSON to Object Lock and stores only the payload_sha256 and row_count in the table. The schema fingerprint must be NORMALISED before hashing — SHOW CREATE ALL TABLES does not guarantee intra-category ordering — and a test must assert the fingerprint is stable across two consecutive computations of an unchanged schema (K2 exit criterion 6).

Write scripts/custody/check_chain_fn_matches_spec.py implementing CU-9: extract the normative fn_permit_event_chain body from spec/custody/chain-verification.md and diff it against the live pg_get_functiondef() output modulo whitespace, failing CI on any drift. It must SKIP with a clear reason when no cluster is reachable, never pass silently. Record the quorum rules in docs/adr/0049-witness-quorum-diversity.md.
workers.done_when: The witness refuses a split view and a shrinking tree, is idempotent on a repeat, and returns a cosignature that trappoint-verify check 7 accepts; the admissibility evaluator is correct across all four (quorum, diversity, adverse, debt) combinations and reports PASS-but-not-adverse at q=1; the schema fingerprint is byte-stable across two consecutive computations; a missing ccloud JSON field is a hard failure; and check_chain_fn_matches_spec.py fails on a mutated function body and SKIPs with a reason when no cluster is reachable.

workers.title: The stranger-verifiable reference bundle, the fifteen-attack nemesis harness, ATTACK-DEPTH
workers.brief:
Read BUILD_PLAN.md K2 exit criteria and Proof; ARCHITECTURE.md §7.5 (three tiers; the README leads with Tier 2 because Tier 2 needs nothing from anyone); docs/leads/custody.md §1.5 and CU-6. This worker turns the whole domain into something a stranger runs in 30 seconds and a hostile expert cannot dismiss.

Build evidence/reference-ledger/: generate.py produces a complete, byte-deterministic signed bundle — fixed clock, uuid5 identities under a fixed namespace, a committed P-256 key at keys/reference-log.NOT-SECRET.key.pem — containing at least 64 leaves across several entry_kinds, every consecutive-checkpoint consistency proof, inclusion proofs for a named subset, receipts, a schema_attestation with pg_get_triggerdef text, closure generation rows for check 14, a WebAuthn assertion for check 12, and locally-minted TSA tokens plus recorded (fixture) S3 object-lock metadata. Commit bundle.json and MANIFEST.sha256. The directory README must carry, verbatim, the sentence 'this key is public by design — the reference bundle proves the verifier works, not that MAINLINE's production log is honest', and must show the one command a stranger runs: `uvx trappoint-verify verify --bundle evidence/reference-ledger/bundle.json`. CI asserts regeneration is a zero-diff no-op, mirroring `trappoint render`.

Build tests/integration/custody/nemesis/: fifteen executable attacks against a DISPOSABLE single-node Docker CockroachDB and a working copy of the bundle — A1 delete_and_relink (delete leaf k, renumber k+1..n and recompute every link_hash in one UPDATE ... FROM generate_series: this is the attack the whole design exists for), A2 renumber_only, A3 payload_substitute, A4 canon_substitute, A5 canon_version_downgrade, A6 fork, A7 checkpoint_swap, A8 backdate_forward, A9 backdate_backward, A10 closure_mass_rewrite (S2), A11 prev_digest_forgery (S9), A12 sandbox_smuggle, A13 trigger_disable, A14 receipt_orphan, A15 object_lock_downgrade. Each attack runs the full verifier and records which checks FAILed and how long detection took. A conftest fixture must REFUSE any DSN whose host is not localhost or 127.0.0.1 — a nemesis suite that can reach production is itself a T1 attack surface.

Emit evidence/CUSTODY_ATTACK_MATRIX.md: attack x detecting check x detection latency, generated not hand-written, cross-referenced to spec/custody/attacks.yaml. CI FAILS if any attack is detected by zero checks and FLAGS (does not fail) any detected by exactly one — this is the custody analogue of the kernel's refusal-depth matrix and it is the artefact that goes on screen. A15 reports SKIP(no-credentials) today and must appear in the matrix as skipped, never be silently absent.

Write .github/workflows/custody-chain.yml running, in order: the jcs vectors, the merkle properties, the verifier dependency-floor and no-network tests, the vendored-canon equality, the reference-bundle zero-diff regeneration, the reference-bundle verification in a CLEAN venv with only cryptography installed (proving Tier 1), the sequencer concurrency job against a service container, the nemesis matrix, check_evidence_plan.py and check_chain_fn_matches_spec.py. Do not name the file custody.yml — the kernel lead owns the eight base workflows. Do not edit tests/integration/custody/test_k2_exit.py; make it green by building artefacts.
